name: MINT-1T
description: MINT-1T is the most extensive and diverse open-source Multimodal INTerleaved dataset comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images. The dataset includes previously untapped sources such as PDFs and ArXiv papers, sourced from HTML documents, PDFs, and ArXiv papers from CommonCrawl and ArXiv dumps.
publisher: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley
citeAs: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt. MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271v5 [cs.CV] 31 Oct 2024
rai:dataCollection: MINT-1T curates multimodal documents from three sources: (1) HTML documents extracted from CommonCrawl WARC files from May 2017 to April 2024 by parsing DOM trees, (2) PDF documents sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024, downloaded and parsed using PyMuPDF with reading order extraction, and (3) ArXiv documents built from LaTeX source code using TexSoup to identify figure tags and interleave images with paper text.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) CommonCrawl WARC files for HTML documents from May 2017 to April 2024 (full dumps from October 2018 to April 2024 and partial dumps from earlier years), (2) CommonCrawl WAT files for PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024, and (3) ArXiv LaTeX source code from ArXiv S3 buckets.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection timeframe: January 2024 to June 2024. Web data included spans from 2013 to 2024, with HTML documents from May 2017 to April 2024 and PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For HTML documents, DOM trees were parsed from WARC entries. For PDFs, reading order was obtained by finding bounding boxes of text blocks, clustering blocks based on columns, and ordering from top left to bottom right. Images were anchored based on proximity between image bounding boxes and text blocks. For ArXiv, main Tex files were identified and input tags were replaced with file contents, with cleanup removing imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included multiple stages: (1) Text quality filtering: Non-English documents removed using Fasttext language identification (confidence threshold 0.65), URLs with NSFW substrings removed, documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or low quality per MassiveText rules removed. (2) Image filtering: Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels removed, aspect ratio filtering (>2 for HTML, >3 for PDFs). (3) Document filtering: HTML documents with no images or more than 30 images removed, PDFs over 50MB or 50 pages excluded, pages with no text discarded. (4) Safety filtering: NSFW image detector applied, documents with single NSFW image discarded, email addresses and IP addresses anonymized. (5) Deduplication: Paragraph and document text deduplication using Bloom Filter (false positive rate 0.01) on 13-gram paragraphs, documents with >80% duplicate paragraphs discarded, exact paragraph deduplication on 2% of each snapshot for boilerplate removal, image deduplication removing images appearing >10 times per snapshot.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fasttext language identification model, NSFW image detector (https://github.com/GantMan/nsfw_model), PyMuPDF for PDF parsing, TexSoup for ArXiv LaTeX parsing
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be actively maintained by the authors who will respond to issues. Updates will be communicated through the README in the Huggingface interface. Older versions will be available through Git history. An erratum will be present on the Huggingface dataset page. A Google form will be provided for data removal requests. The dataset is planned for release in July 2024 and will be distributed as JSON shards through Huggingface.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain sensitive information as it is sourced from the public web, including data that reveals race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, locations, and images of individuals. Steps were taken to mask personally identifiable information including email addresses and IP addresses. The dataset respects robots.txt files from CommonCrawl.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T was built to make research into large multimodal models more accessible. Inappropriate use cases include training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information (such as images of people's faces and other sensitive content) as well as military applications. While the dataset is freely available under CC-BY-4.0 license, users are responsible for ensuring its legal use in commercial settings and must independently verify compliance with applicable laws.
rai:dataBiases: The authors follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. The dataset may contain biases present in web data. Domain analysis using LDA revealed that OBELICS shows pronounced concentration in 'Humanities and Social Sciences' while MINT-1T's HTML subset is more balanced across domains, and the PDF subset has higher proportion of 'Science and Technology' documents.
rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) PDF parsing issues - sometimes unable to detect images and incorrect reading order extraction across diverse document layouts due to arbitrary PDF layouts, (2) While steps were taken to remove harmful content, offensive content may still be present, (3) Image URLs rely on external resources with no guarantees of continued availability due to link rot, (4) The full dataset is over 300TB making it infeasible to host with images included, (5) Future work should explore more ways to improve safety of multimodal internet data and develop fast, robust methods for determining reading order across diverse document layouts.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for pre-training large multimodal models (LMMs) that can process multiple interleaved images and text. Experiments show LMMs trained on MINT-1T rival the performance of models trained on OBELICS. The dataset can be used for training objectives like generating interleaved images and text sequences or for building multimodal document retrieval systems. Training data usage: 50% image-text captioning batches and 50% multimodal interleaved batches, with maximum of 2048 multimodal tokens sampled from each interleaved document.
